sanskrit: nāśaya palitaṃ śīrṣṇo yaḥ kṛṣṇas tan na ā bhara | tam oṣadhe tvaṃ vardhaya keśaṃ kṛṣṇataraṃ kṛdhi ||
english: Destroy the grey hair of the head; bring back that which is black. O herb, make it grow — render the hair yet blacker.

sanskrit: yathāñjanaṃ tathāsasi yathā traikakudaṃ tathā | tat saṃbhavāt tat sabhas te vyucchantīr anūṣasaḥ ||
english: As is collyrium, so art thou; as is the three-peaked plant, so art thou. From that origin, from that assembly of thine — the dawns that shine forth, one after another.

sanskrit: yatrāsti yatra tiṣṭhati yato naśyatvāsinam | divyaḥ suparṇo abravīd etat palitabheṣajam ||
english: Where it exists, where it stands, from where let it vanish — the sword-like thing: the divine eagle has declared this to be the remedy for grey hair.

sanskrit: divo nu mā bṛhato antarikṣād apāṃ stoko abhy apaptad rasāya | sam indriyeṇa payasā ham agne ṛṣīṇāṃ yajñaiḥ sukṛtāṃ kṛtena ||
english: From the vast sky, from the atmosphere, a drop of waters fell upon me for the sake of the sap. Unite me, O Agni, with vital power and with milk, through the sacrifices of the seers and through the deeds of the virtuous.

sanskrit: yadi vṛkṣād abhy apaptat phalaṃ tad yady antarikṣāt tad u vāyur eva | yatrāspṛṣṭa tanvo yatra vāsaso na tat prāpnoti nirṛtiḥ parastāt ||
english: If that fruit fell from a tree, if it fell from the atmosphere, that too is but the wind. Where the body is untouched, where the garment is untouched — there Dissolution does not reach from beyond.

sanskrit: abhyañjanaṃ surabhyād u vāsaś candraṃ hiraṇyam adhi pūtrimaṃ yat | sarvā pavitrā vitatādhy asmiṃc chataṃ jīvāti śaradas tavāyam ||
english: The ointment is fragrant, and so is the garment; bright is the gold upon it, purified. All the purifying strainers are spread over this one — let him live a hundred autumns; this is thine.

sanskrit: yaḥ kīkasāḥ praśṛṇāti talīḍyam upatiṣṭhati | parāsthaṃ sarvaṃ jāyānyaṃ yaḥ kaś ca kakubhi śritaḥ ||
english: He who shatters the spine, who approaches with licking — all the jāyānya standing afar, and whatever jāyānya has taken refuge in the corners of the sky.

sanskrit: pakṣī jāyānyaḥ patati ya āviśati pūruṣam | tasyāhaṃ veda te nāma yato jāyānya jāyase ||
english: The jāyānya is a bird that flies and enters a man. I know thy name, O jāyānya — the place from which thou art born.

sanskrit: veda vai te nāma yato jāyānya jāyase | kathaṃ hi tatra tvaṃ hanyā yat kuryām ahaṃ haviḥ ||
english: I know indeed thy name, the place from which thou, O jāyānya, art born. How then couldst thou strike there, if I were to make an oblation?

sanskrit: ya āsyaṃ praviśati karoty udaraṃ mahat | yakṣmo yo atra jāyase taṃ jāyānyam anīnaśam ||
english: He who enters the mouth and makes the belly large — the disease that is born here, that jāyānya I have utterly destroyed.

sanskrit: ārohān me mukhaṃ jātam ārohāj jaghanaṃ mama | ārohāt sarvā jātāsmy ṛṣabhasyopayodhanāt ||
english: From the ārohā plant my mouth is born; from the ārohā plant are my loins. From the ārohā plant I am wholly born — from the coupling of the bull.

sanskrit: svādīyasī surāyā lavaṇāc cārumattarā | gobhyo vanīyasīd aham ||
english: Sweeter than liquor, more pleasing than salt — I am more desirable than the cows.

sanskrit: yāṃ tvā vāto 'vārayad ārdranābhā maharṣabhaḥ | tasyās te devi pṛthivyā ahaṃ saṃvananaṃ dada ā te śauṣkāsyaṃ dade ||
english: The great bull with the moist navel held thee back — thee, O wind. To thee, O divine Earth, I give the act of attraction; I take away thy dryness of mouth.

sanskrit: yuktau manasā saṃ suretasā devebhyo havyaṃ kṛṇavāva sādhu | yeṣāṃ bhāgas ta idaṃ juṣantām avikṣubdhāv udayāva bhadrayā ||
english: United in mind, united in good seed, let the two of us offer the oblation well to the gods. Let those whose portion this is delight in it. Let the two of us rise up together, undisturbed, with good fortune.

sanskrit: yena devā jyotiṣā dyām udāyan yenādityā vasavo yena rudrāḥ | yenāṅgirasaḥ svar āruruhus tenod ayāva yajamānau svasti ||
english: By that light by which the gods rose to heaven, by which the Ādityas, the Vasus, and the Rudras rose, by which the Aṅgirases ascended to the sun — by that let the two sacrificers rise up in well-being.

sanskrit: yaṃ papācāditiḥ putrakāmā yena prajāḥ kaśyapaḥ paryagṛhnāt | ya odanaḥ pacyate vaiśvadevaḥ sa no yame akṣito bhāgo astu ||
english: The odana-rice that Aditi cooked when desiring a son, by which Kaśyapa encompassed offspring — the odana that is cooked for all the gods: let our share in it be inexhaustible at the right time.

sanskrit: somasya prāṇaḥ pavate purastād dakṣiṇata aindra ā vātu vātaḥ | asya diśo māturo yā pratīcī sa no devāḥ śivo astv iha vātaḥ ||
english: The breath of Soma blows from the east; from the south let the wind of Indra blow to us. From that direction which is the mother, which is the west — let that wind be auspicious to us here, O gods.

sanskrit: mitrasya prāṇaḥ pavate ya uttarād bṛhaspater ūrdhva ud vātu vātaḥ | yo antarikṣam anu vāti vidvān sa no devaḥ śivo astv iha vātaḥ ||
english: The breath of Mitra blows from the north; upward from Bṛhaspati let the wind blow. That wind which blows knowing the atmosphere — let that god be auspicious to us here.

sanskrit: ya uttarāt pavate yaḥ purastād yo dakṣiṇāt pavate yaś ca paścāt | ūrdhvām̐ uddeśām̐ anu yaḥ pravāti sa no devaḥ śivo astv iha vātaḥ ||
english: He who blows from the north, he who blows from the east, he who blows from the south, and he who blows from the west — he who blows upward in those upper regions: let that god be auspicious to us here.

sanskrit: trīṇy antarikṣāṇy anu vāsi vāta tisro vāsi parāvataḥ | sahasrākṣau vṛtrahā pāhy arvāṅ vinudaṃ kṣetriyaṃ rapaḥ ||
english: O Wind, thou blowest through three atmospheres; thou blowest through three remote distances. O thou of a thousand eyes, slayer of Vṛtra, guard us here; drive away the hereditary disease and blemish.

sanskrit: na tatra dāraḥ kṛpaṇaṃ sasāra na pratighnānā rudatī na bibhratī | indro no yatrorukṛd vicakṣaṇaḥ sa no *'jyāni mahatīṃ ni yacchāt ||
english: There no wife has gone in wretchedness, no one weeping and wailing in resistance, no one carrying a burden. Where Indra, the far-striding and discerning one, stands for us — let him grant us that great safety.

sanskrit: indraḥ senāṃ mohayatu maruto ghnantv ojasā | agner vātasya dhrājyā tān viṣūco vi nāśaya ||
english: Let Indra confuse their army; let the Maruts smite them with might. By the blazing force of Agni and of Wind, scatter them in all directions and destroy them.

sanskrit: na dyaur eṣāṃ na pṛthivī nāditir na dhanaṃjayā | cakṣūṃṣy agnir ā dhattāṃ punar yantu parājitāḥ ||
english: Neither heaven nor earth nor Aditi nor the wealth-winning power is theirs. Let Agni take away their sight; let them go back utterly defeated.

sanskrit: amitrāṇāṃ daraya grāmam indra yo naḥ śatrur abhyeti jighāṃsan | yathaiṣām indranuttānām agninā veśo anu vartayāni me ||
english: O Indra, smash the village of the enemies, the foe who comes against us intending to slay. Just as these are driven away by Indra — so let me turn the settlement with Agni's help.

sanskrit: jihmaṃ yugaṃ kṛṇvatām indranuttāḥ parācīnaiḥ pathibhir yantu riṣyantaḥ | tañ jayanto anv āsadema- -agninā veśo anu vartayantaḥ ||
english: Driven away by Indra, let them make their yoke go crooked; let them go by paths turned away, suffering harm. Conquering them, let us settle upon that, turning the settlement with Agni.

sanskrit: amitrāṇāṃ grāmam upayuktam indreṇa nuttaṃ vi radāty agniḥ | satvānaḥ santv anumādyā ime yebhyaś carāmi haviṣā ghṛtena ||
english: The village of the enemies, attacked and driven away by Indra — Agni splits it open. Let these warriors be worthy of praise, those for whom I proceed with oblation and clarified butter.

sanskrit: aryamaṇaṃ hi devaṃ bhadraṃ kanyā yam ayakṣata | sa enā vṛtrahā deva ito muñcātu māmutaḥ ||
english: Aryaman, the auspicious god whom the maiden worshipped — let that god, the slayer of Vṛtra, release her from here and from that place.

sanskrit: iyaṃ te rājan varuṇa jāmikā kṛṇute haviḥ | tasyai patiṃ ny ā vaha subhadraṃ pratikāmyam ||
english: O King Varuṇa, this kinswoman makes offering to thee. Bring to her a husband who is truly good and desirable.

sanskrit: ā krandaya dhanapate varam āmanasaṃ kṛṇu | sarvaṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛdhi patim asyai pratikāmyam ||
english: O Lord of wealth, make him cry out with longing; make the suitor single-minded. Make everything turn to the right; bring her a husband who is desirable.

sanskrit: ā paścād ā purastād ottarād adharād uta | pūrṇā bhagasya vartanis tenemām abhi vartayāmasi varcasā ca bhagena ca ||
english: From the west and from the east, from the north and from below as well — full is the track of Bhaga; by it we turn this woman toward him, with glory and with good fortune.

sanskrit: nāsṛg asti pataṅgasya tardasya maśakadyāḥ | na saṃpatatram udyugo nyag glaur atra bhaviṣyati ||
english: There is no blood of the moth, of the woodpecker, or of the gnats; there is no collision of flight, no upward effort — the disease will be downcast and gone from here.

sanskrit: apadasvad apādasat tuṇḍivyadhmāpādasat | apāpacid ito 'dasad apeto glaur naśiṣyaty apivyadhman naśiṣyati ||
english: It slunk away footless; footless it departed; puffing with its snout it departed. The evil-cooker too has departed from here. The disease, once gone, will perish; piercing and swelling will likewise perish.

sanskrit: yathā sūryaś candramasam udyann evāpagūhati | evā tvam ugra oṣadha imāṃ glāvam apagūhatād itaḥ ||
english: Just as the sun, rising, conceals the moon — so do thou, O mighty herb, conceal and drive this disease away from here.

sanskrit: apadasvad apādasat tuṇḍivyadhmāpādasat | apāpacid ito 'dasad apeto glaur naśiṣyaty apivyadhman naśiṣyati ||
english: It slunk away footless; footless it departed; puffing with its snout it departed. The evil-cooker too has departed from here. The disease, once gone, will perish; piercing and swelling will likewise perish.

sanskrit: mā śile mā śilāvati mā te śeṣi śilaṃ cana | yāvac chilasya te śilaṃ tāvac cheṣaḥ śilaṃ tava ||
english: Not on stone, not on what has stone, let not even a sliver of stone remain for thee. As much stone as there is of thy stone — so much is the residue of stone that is thine.

sanskrit: yathā yūpāgrād udakaṃ viniṣṭaṃ bhūmim aśnute | evā tvam arase śile viniṣṭā bhūmim aśnuhi ||
english: Just as water poured out from the top of the sacrificial post reaches the ground — so do thou, O sapless stone, having been poured out, reach the ground.

sanskrit: vajro 'si sapatnahā tvayādya vṛtraṃ sākṣīya | tvām adya vanaspate vṛkṣāṇām ud ayuṣmahi ||
english: Thou art the thunderbolt, the slayer of rivals — with thee today I would overcome Vṛtra. Thee, O Lord of the forest, chief of trees, today we lift up for long life.

sanskrit: sa na indra purohito viśvatas pāhi rakṣasaḥ | abhi gāvo anūṣata- -abhi dyumnaṃ bṛhaspate ||
english: Thou, Indra, as our foremost priest, guard us from the demon on all sides. The cows have lowed in accord — in accord with the glory, O Bṛhaspati.

sanskrit: prāṇa prāṇaṃ trāyasva- -aso asave mṛḍa | nirṛte nirṛtyā naḥ pāśebhyo muñca ||
english: O Breath, protect breath; be gracious to the living soul for the sake of the breath of life. O Nirṛti, by thy dissolution, release us from the bonds.

sanskrit: hatsuke pari ṇo nama pārigaṃ tanve kṛdhi | yuyuta parṇinaṃ śaram utāparṇaṃ riśād iti ||
english: O Hatsuka, bow around us; make a girding for our bodies. Keep away the arrow that carries leaf, and likewise the leafless one that wounds.

sanskrit: prajāpatiṣ ṭvā prajayā saṃ putreṇa sṛjatu saṃ bhagena | diṣṭaṃ deṣṭīha kāmo brāhmaṇasya pumāṃsaṃ dhatsva savituḥ savena ||
english: Let Prajāpati unite thee with offspring, with a son, with good fortune. Let destiny guide thee here; the desire of the brahmin impels — place a male within her by the impulsion of Savitṛ.

sanskrit: pra tvā sarpatv aṅkataḥ kumāraḥ puruṣād adhi | ṛtor yam ṛtviyād adhi yaṃ te dhātā acīkl̥pat ||
english: Let the boy creep forth from thee, from the curve, from above a man. According to the season, above the seasonable one — him whom Dhātṛ fashioned for thee.

sanskrit: yaṃ te dhātā yaṃ te tvaṣṭā yaṃ te brahmācīkl̥pat | taṃ tvaṃ putraṃ vindasva tasmai tvaṃ jīva jīvase ||
english: Whom Dhātṛ fashioned for thee, whom Tvaṣṭṛ fashioned for thee, whom the brahmin power fashioned for thee — find that son; for his sake live thou to live.

sanskrit: dhvasrās tiṣṭhanti rajasā samaktā yajñasya hotrāḥ pruśitāso aśnāḥ | āsāṃ somasya yad ihāvayanti tad amūtra yajamānasya rūpam ||
english: The brilliant ones stand smeared with dust, the hotrī-priests of the sacrifice dripping with the stones. Whatever of Soma they pour down here — that is the form of the sacrificer yonder.

sanskrit: ye brāhmaṇaṃ varco hitvāya malvā reṇo varṇena paridhāpayanti | āsāṃ somasya yad ihāvayanti tad amūtra yajamānasya rūpam ||
english: Those who, having abandoned the luster of the brahmin, clothe him with dust and dirt as his color — whatever of Soma they pour down here, that is the form of the sacrificer yonder.

sanskrit: asārathiḥ sumanaso yathā ratho hitvā savyaṣṭhāṃ rakṣaso yāti yāmam | evā yajño yajamānaṃ jahāti yatra somyaṃ somapīthān nayanti ||
english: Just as a well-appointed chariot without a charioteer, abandoning its left yoke-horse, goes on the course of demons — so the sacrifice forsakes the sacrificer when they lead the Soma-rite to those who drink Soma improperly.

sanskrit: chandāṃsi tad yajamānasya yanti yatra somyaṃ somapīthān nayanti | abrāhmaṇo yat pibati somam asya tad vai chidraṃ dakṣiṇayāpidheyam ||
english: The Vedic meters go away from the sacrificer when they lead the Soma-rite to those who drink Soma improperly. When a non-brahmin drinks the Soma — that is indeed a breach, to be covered over with the sacrificial fee.

sanskrit: 'bradhno 'si vājī paripānī prathamā devebhyas paryābhṛtā | mā te riṣaṃ khanitā yasmai ca tvā khanāmasi ||
english: Thou art the ruddy one, the swift one, the all-encompassing drink, first brought around for the gods. May the digger suffer no harm — nor he for whom we dig thee.

sanskrit: mā devāḥ pāpam ārāma mā karta pāpayāmuyā | māhaṃ pariṣyajo hastam ā rapsi dhanakāmyā ||
english: O gods, let us not reach evil; do not lead us by the path of evil. May I not wound the hand of my companion in my desire for wealth.

sanskrit: mā mā devāḥ parā dāta mā mā karta vyādhyam | māhaṃ pariṣvajaḥ śira ā rapsi mo ahaṃ mṛṣi ||
english: O gods, do not give me over; do not make me sick. May I not wound the head of my companion; may I not err.
